correctness.rationale: The all-positive and all-negative traces force a forest and connected complement; extending any desired positive subforest in the complement plus that subforest suffices. The negative trace bounds the support size by six. An independent standard-library replay built KG(5,2), generated all connected nine-edge subsets by graph flood fill, and compared the actual traces against the forest (leaf stripping) and connected-complement predicates. It reproduced 2000 trees, face counts (1,15,105,445,1230,2160,1930), purity with 1930 six-edge facets, the 60 five-cycle-plus-edge and 10 six-cycle exclusions, all 19 orbit representatives and the 30,40,60^3,120^14 orbit census, and the three failed exchanges 111,126,8302 for A=238, B=8283 and removed edge 7. The full automorphism group acts on the five size-four independent sets, which are exactly the five stars of pairs through one symbol: any intersecting family with two pairs 12,13 and a pair omitting 1 is confined to the triangle 12,13,23. Each vertex is determined by its two incident stars, so the natural S5 already gives the full action.
residual_risks: The enumeration is exhaustive for the specified 15-edge graph only; no claim of formal verification or of generalization to other graphs.

value.rationale: This is a canonical highly symmetric cubic graph and a natural exact incidence-shattering invariant, not an arbitrary test case. The facet-orbit list gives reusable explicit types, and purity together with an exact exchange failure separates two natural independence properties in a case where neither is answered by the general criterion. The full count and cycle exclusions are useful small-instance benchmarks for common graphic/cographic independence.
residual_risks: Value is as a complete census and obstruction on Petersen, not a scalable new algorithm or a graph-family theorem.
